skill.name: proxy-benchmark
skill.description: Guides proxy and browser benchmarking with an external Python harness, including provider comparisons, success rates, traffic costs, and reproducible run reports.
skill.summary: Plan proxy comparisons, configure browser engines, and interpret benchmark results with documented commands.
skill.author: nodemaven

security_audit.summary: All 36 static findings are false positives involving Markdown, example configuration, legitimate setup commands, or ordinary prose. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, malicious scheduling, or unauthorized reconnaissance in SKILL.md. The external benchmark repository and its dependencies were not included, so their runtime behavior remains unverified.

remediation.issue: Setup instructions do not specify an immutable harness revision or dependency integrity checks.
remediation.suggestion: As a precaution, document a reviewed commit and verified dependency versions before asking users to install or execute the external harness.

remediation.issue: Credential configuration guidance does not specify local file permissions or credential scope.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend restricted file permissions, narrowly scoped proxy credentials, and exclusion of credentials and raw responses from version control.

content.user_title: Compare Proxy Providers and Browser Engines
content.value_statement: Proxy performance and traffic costs vary across targets, engines, and measurement times. This skill guides controlled comparisons and result interpretation using an external benchmark harness.
actual_capabilities: Provides setup commands for the external Python harness and a small direct HTTP benchmark.
Explains provider credentials, custom proxy settings, and provider configuration templates.
Documents interleaved provider comparisons, engine comparisons, and direct browser baselines.
Explains query counts, batch sizes, country selection, resource presets, resume behavior, and failure limits.
Documents gateway health checks, dry-run planning, and traffic-cost analysis.
Guides interpretation of run reports, individual result rows, and reproducibility evidence.
limitations: The skill contains instructions only; the executable harness and its dependencies require a separate checkout and installation.
Python 3.11 or later is required, and browser engines need additional installation.
Proxy runs require user-supplied credentials and can consume paid bandwidth; direct runs expose the user's network address to targets.
Benchmark results depend on targets, timing, geography, and configuration; successful access and published performance numbers are not guaranteed.

use_cases.title: Compare proxy providers
use_cases.description: Plan an interleaved comparison with matching targets, query counts, and browser settings before selecting a provider.

use_cases.title: Evaluate browser engines
use_cases.description: Compare supported browser engines with a direct baseline and identify which configurations serve the selected target.

use_cases.title: Review performance evidence
use_cases.description: Interpret run reports, inspect individual attempts, and relate reported success rates to traffic costs and measurement dates.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a first benchmark
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a five-query direct HTTP benchmark for DuckDuckGo. Show prerequisites and the dry-run plan, then wait for approval before sending requests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: a small run without proxy credentials or browser installation.

prompt_templates.title: Configure a custom proxy
prompt_templates.prompt: Explain custom proxy configuration and the gateway health check. Use placeholders, keep credentials local, and ask before making network requests.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: prepare a user-owned proxy gateway without exposing credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Compare two providers
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan an interleaved comparison of two providers on an authorized target. Match engine, country, queries, and batch size; show estimated cost before execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: compare providers under equivalent conditions.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze engines and cost
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an engine comparison with a direct baseline, resource presets, failure limits, and request pacing. Use dry-run planning and report results only from supplied runs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert: evaluate engine behavior and cost while preserving reproducibility.

output_examples.input: Plan a small direct HTTP test before I install browser engines.
output: Plan: five queries using HTTP, direct networking, and no resource blocking.
Prerequisites: Python 3.11 or later and the external harness with core dependencies.
Status: planning only; no requests sent and no benchmark results claimed.

output_examples.input: Can I compare provider A this morning with provider B this afternoon?
output: Different measurement windows can confound the comparison.
Interleave both providers with matching engine, target, country, query count, and batch size.
Review the dry-run cost estimate and retain the run file and measurement date.
No performance ranking is available without measured results.

best_practices: Review the harness revision and dependencies, then preview each new matrix with a dry run before approving traffic and costs.
Interleave comparisons, match settings, pause at least three to five seconds between requests, and cite run files with dates.
Keep credentials and raw responses local, restrict credential access, and mask identifiers before sharing results.
anti_patterns: Treating a single run or measurements from different time windows as a definitive provider ranking.
Retrying repeatedly after target refusals or increasing request volume without reviewing cost and failure limits.
Publishing environment files, proxy credentials, unmasked identifiers, or raw response bodies.

faq.question: Does this skill include the benchmark program?
faq.answer: No. It provides instructions for a separate open-source Python harness that must be cloned and installed.

faq.question: Can I start without a paid proxy?
faq.answer: Yes. The documented first run uses direct HTTP requests without proxy credentials or browser installation.

faq.question: Which targets are documented?
faq.answer: The skill lists Google, Bing, DuckDuckGo, Amazon search, and an exit-IP target.

faq.question: Can it compare browser engines?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents multiple engines and direct baselines, but engines require installation and may be unavailable on your machine.

faq.question: How should I manage traffic costs?
faq.answer: Preview the matrix with a dry run, start with small query counts, retain failure limits, and use the documented cost-analysis tools.

faq.question: Are credentials or benchmark results uploaded?
faq.answer: The instructions keep environment files and raw responses local. The external harness was not audited here, so its runtime behavior remains unverified.
